svg.aria-label: Skylo Regional Hub VPC architecture in us-west-2: internet traffic enters through an IGW and NLB into a three-AZ public tier (NAT plus NLB), routes into a three-AZ private tier running EKS with per-AZ route tables, attaches to a Transit Gateway that splits Ground (DX) and Org (east-west) traffic, and reaches the on-prem Ground Station network or Skylo Org accounts.
svg.text: Three-tier hub VPC: public ingress/egress → private EKS compute → Transit Gateway segmentation → on-prem ground network + org accounts
NLB — PUBLIC SURFACE (single internet-facing entry point)

svg.text: Private: EKS nodes + pods, no public IPs.
Blast radius: public tier can never reach
Each AZ's private subnet points to its own
NAT gateway (not a shared cross-AZ NAT).
If AZ-a fails, AZ-b / AZ-c keep independent
Two separate TGW route tables: Ground (DX)
Hub VPC advertises both routes; the TGW
decides which table each packet hits.
Ground vs. org traffic isolated at the TGW
layer — not mixed in one route table.
No pod reaches the internet directly — all
not compete with node IP space.
Karpenter scales nodes, HPA scales pods —
independent scaling on two address spaces.
New hubs stay collision-free by construction.
b) Ground Station → DX → AWS DX endpoint → TGW
c) TGW matches 10.200.0.0/16 in Ground RT
d) TGW forwards into hub VPC attachment
e) Private subnet receives on TGW-attach ENI
g) Core-network pod queries Redis, decides route
h) UPF pod forwards to the NLB
i) NLB → IGW → response to customer
